consensus_summary: Consensus primary meaning is sand as an innumerable multitude (esp. Abrahamic descendants, peoples, armies); a common separate alternative is sand as an unstable/foolish foundation (Matt 7); minority/rare senses include divine sea-boundary and heaviness.
book_summary: Book: countless multitude and, as foundation, instability of building on the crowd rather than the covenant Rock—people not bound together by a covenant (opposite: Rock).
consensus_core_identification: Innumerable multitude (primary); unstable foundation as a distinct common alternative.
book_core_identification: Countless multitude; when foundation, building on the non-covenant crowd versus the covenant Rock.
boundary_disagreement: Consensus treats multitude and Matt 7 foundation as separate context-bound senses; the book unifies them by reading foundation-sand specifically as the crowd/people unbound by covenant, not generic instability.
material_contradiction: None; the book does not deny multitude or foundation instability, but specializes the latter referent.
rationale: Minimum cores overlap on multitude and on sand-as-bad-foundation. Difference is boundary/precision: book reinterprets Matt 7 sand as the multitude/crowd opposed to covenant Rock, narrowing and linking what consensus keeps as independent readings. That is refinement, not core replacement or novelty.
strongest_objection: Matt 7 sand need not mean 'the crowd' or non-covenant people; consensus may hold foundation instability without equating it to the multitude symbol.
